title: LED Inspection - Bridge Defects Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Pre-Diffusion Quality Validation for 22nm Node Manufacturing
author: Robert Kim

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Bridge Defects defects during pre-diffusion inspection at the 22nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Bridge Defects defects that are critical to yield at the 22nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: LED Inspection
- Target Defect: Bridge Defects
- Process Step: Pre-Diffusion
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 22nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for pre-diffusion monitoring in the 22nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v14.0.148
Recipe: LED_INSPECTION_22nm_PRE_DIFFUSION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (198 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'LED Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Bridge Defects defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 22nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 56 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.9% for LED Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.97 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-07
Wafers Tested: 13
Total Defects Found: 3943
Defect Density: 1255.1 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.1%
Capture Rate: 89.7%
Test Duration: 73 minutes
System Uptime: 98.8%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Bridge Defects at the 22nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
